entities.summary: Medius of Larissa was a pivotal figure in the Hellenistic era, serving as an officer and friend of Alexander the Great. He played a significant role in the conquests of Alexander, participating in battles such as the Siege of Tyre and the Battle of the Granicus. After Alexander's death, Medius served under Antigonus I Monophthalmus, a senior commander who would go on to shape the Hellenistic world. Medius' legacy extends to the city of Larissa, which he helped establish as a major center of culture and learning. The city's founding is attributed to the transfer of the legendary founder of Larissa, Oxythemis, to the site by Medius, solidifying the city's importance in the region. Medius' story offers a glimpse into the complex web of alliances and rivalries that characterized the Hellenistic period, a time of great cultural and philosophical exchange.
